findings.classification: actual productive-effort gating; export/domestic trade semantics not represented
findings.interpretation: False zeroes site productive effort on an otherwise normal local workday. It does not clear or prohibit arrivals; orders become backlog and have no origin/destination/export-required field. Existing two published engineering profiles both set True, so this control is not proof those engineering runs encountered the False branch.
findings.minimal_r4_semantic_route: Keep local calendar independent of export eligibility. Introduce explicit order market/destination or export-required classification and reject only ineligible cross-border fulfillment while retaining domestic work. Freeze declared synthetic domestic/export composition separately; validate zero-export/positive-domestic and blocked-export backlog/expiry tests. If no trade classification is implemented, label False only as full-site productive shutdown, not export-control realism.

findings.classification: bounded behavioral reservation, not merely numerical overflow validation
findings.interpretation: The bounded time reservation can be a deliberate capacity assumption. However, requested cost above .4 disappears from operational consequences: the method returns only the capped fraction and no unmet coordination backlog/service loss. This masks further marginal scale/structure cost for saturated configurations; it does not imply every larger organization saturates, because guild inventory/report span and communication also matter.
findings.minimal_r4_semantic_route: Retain a feasible day budget, expose requested/served/unmet coordination separately, and give unmet coordination an explicit validated operational consequence (queue/delay or service loss) in a separately frozen candidate. Removing min(.4) alone is not evidence of realistic coordination. Until such a mechanism is validated, limit claims to a saturating coordination reservation rather than unrestricted large-scale coordination-cost realism.

findings.classification: conservative cash-safe output allocation used as actual production policy
findings.interpretation: Max-site unit cost is safe against overspending, and the finite-arithmetic configuration envelope at 104–109 legitimately uses a conservative bound. But the same max at 201 is behaviorally applied to all production. A costly installed site with zero productive potential can suppress output at a cheap site despite an available feasible allocation. This is underutilization, not a demonstrated ledger conservation failure.
findings.minimal_r4_semantic_route: Compute per-site potential p_s before allocation and its actual unit cost c_s=material+logistics_s. For a declared uniform scaling policy use f=min(1,backlog/sum(p_s),capacity*units_per_seat/sum(p_s),cash/sum(p_s*c_s)), with explicit zero-denominator handling; scale each p_s by the same f, so idle sites contribute zero cost. Preserve strict finish_day actual-cost and stock-conservation gates. Keep the maximum-context cost for numerical representability/preflight bounds only; alternative site-priority allocation would require a separately declared policy.
